titleEn: Book of the Dead of Ani — Spell 147, the seven gates, part 2
part: Spell 147 — the seven gates: the fourth to the seventh gate (Plates 11–12)
about: This part gives the second half of Spell 147, the fourth to the seventh of the gates (ꜥryt) of the realm of Osiris, along the upper register of Plates 11 and 12 of Ani's papyrus. At each gate the dead man names its doorkeeper, watcher and announcer, and then tells what he has done for Osiris: he has brought him life and the parts of his body, driven off Apep, and protected the god's eye. Budge numbers the lines afresh in each gate. Most of the gatekeepers' names and several phrases are doubtful, and the speech at the sixth gate breaks off where Budge prints a row of dots.

sentences.i: The fourth gate.
sentences.n: ꜥryt 'gate' as in the first part of the spell: the arm ꜥ, r, two reeds and t, with the house sign as classifier (Budge: ārit, 'hall'). fdnwt 'fourth' is four strokes, the numeral four (fdw), with the pot nw and t: the ordinal fdnw, which adds -nw to the numeral, feminine to agree with ꜥryt (Budge: àft). This unit opens the fourth gate. Budge starts his line numbers again at 1 in each gate, and the fourth gate runs over his lines 1 to 9. As at the first three gates, the dead man names the gate's doorkeeper, watcher and announcer, and then speaks.

sentences.i: The name of its doorkeeper: Khesef-her-asha-kheru.
sentences.n: rn n iry-ꜥꜣ·s 'the name of its doorkeeper' as at the first gate: rn with the man with hand to mouth (A2) as classifier; the genitive n; the herdsman sign for iry, the sign coded O29 (approximate) for ꜥꜣ 'door', the low sign U15 (not read) and ·s, the gate's. The name is two of Budge's groups, joined here as one word. ḫsf is the spindle-and-viper sign ḫsf (U35) with U15, 'repel, drive back'; ḥr 'face' is the face with its stroke and a seated god; ꜥšꜣ 'many' is the lizard with plural strokes (Budge's numeral 3 is printed after it); ḫrw 'voice' is the oar with w and the man with hand to mouth. 'Repelling of face, many of voices' (?) follows the words (Budge: χesef-ḥrà-āśt-χeru), perhaps a noisy keeper who turns faces away; the sense of the whole is doubtful.

sentences.i: The name of the watcher: Seres-tep.
sentences.n: The papyrus writes rn n in red. sꜣwty 'watcher' is the herdsman sign sꜣw with ꜣ, two reeds y, t and the low sign U15, as at the second gate, but no ·s 'its' is written here. The name is the bolt s and an upright with a hook at the top (coded T13, approximate, as for the third gate's watcher) for rs 'wake', with the eye as classifier: srs 'make watchful'; then the head tp with a stroke, a second stroke and the seated god (Budge: Se-res-ṭepu, reading the strokes as -u). 'Watchful of head' (?) on the pattern of srs-ḥr at the third gate; the reading rests on the same uncertain sign.

sentences.i: The name of the announcer in it: Khesef-ad.
sentences.n: The papyrus writes rn n in red. smi 'announcer' is written here with the bolt s over the lung-and-windpipe sign sm, then a reed and the man with hand to mouth. im·s 'in it' is a reed and m, here the sign Aa15, with ·s. The name (after Budge's numeral 6) is ḫsf 'repel' (U35 with U15), then ꜣ and the hand d with a small crocodile (coded I3, approximate) and the seated god: ꜣd 'be aggressive, rage', which takes the crocodile as its classifier. 'Who repels the raging one' (?) (Budge: χesef-Aṭ).

sentences.l: said · by · the-Osiris · the-scribe · Ani · true-of-voice
sentences.i: Said by the Osiris, the scribe Ani, true of voice:
sentences.n: ḏd in N 'said by N' brings in the speech, as at the earlier gates; here it is in black. ḏd is the cobra and the hand, printed as one sign (coded I10 D46, the house reading), and in is a reed and water n. wsir ꜣny 'the Osiris Ani' names the dead man as an Osiris: the throne and the eye, and Ani's name ending in the squatting man with a flail (A52). sš 'scribe' is the scribe's palette, water pot and pen case alone. mꜣꜥ-ḫrw 'true of voice' is the plinth and the oar, without the sickle, as before.

sentences.l: I · the-bull · son · of-the-kite · of · Osiris
sentences.i: I am the bull, the son of the kite of Osiris.
sentences.n: The speech begins. ink 'I am' is the pot and the basket, here with a bold stroke in place of the seated man. kꜣ 'bull' is the raised arms kꜣ (D28) with the low sign U15 under them and the bull as classifier (Budge: ka). sꜣ 'son' is the pintail duck with its stroke, the noun before a direct genitive. ḏryt is a bundle sign (coded M36, approximate) for ḏr, with r, two reeds y and t, and a bird (coded G39, approximate, like the duck of sꜣ; a bird of prey would be expected): ḏryt 'kite', the bird of prey, the form in which Isis mourns Osiris (Budge: t'erit, 'the ancestress'). nt is the genitive in its feminine form, agreeing with ḏryt. The bull, son of Isis, is Horus, and the dead man speaks as Horus, Osiris's son and helper.

sentences.l: see-you · bears-witness · for-him · father-his · the-lord · of-company-his(?)
sentences.i: See, his father bears witness for him, the lord of his company(?).
sentences.n: m·tn 'see, behold' is the owl m with the arm (printed at its upper right, not read, as in mk), then t and n with plural strokes: the particle mk in the form used to more than one person, here the beings of the gate (Budge reads mā-ten, as a request). Budge's group meter-nef is split here into mtr and n·f. mtr is the hooked sign coded D53 (the house reading, approximate) for mt, with t, r, two strokes and the man with hand to mouth, the classifier of speech: mtr 'bear witness', a sḏm·f whose subject, itf·f 'his father', comes after the dative n·f 'for him' (water n and the viper, the viper restored by Budge inside his square brackets). itf·f is a reed, t and f with the seated man, and ·f. The n could instead be the n of a sḏm·n·f, 'he has borne witness'; n·f 'for him' gives the clearer sense. nb 'the lord' is the basket. imw·f is a reed, a tree-like sign (coded M1) read im, m, w (Budge's numeral 8 stands before it), the seated god with a stroke, and ·f: taken as a plural noun for the beings around a god, 'his company' (Budge: àmmu, 'divine companions'); the reading and the sense are doubtful. The father is Osiris, and 'him' is the speaker, his son.

sentences.i: I have judged the guilty(?) there.
sentences.n: wḏꜥ·n·i is w, the cobra ḏ, a thin flat sign coded D36 for ꜥ, and the sign wḏꜥ (Aa21) closing the word as its classifier, then water n and the seated man: the sḏm·n·f of wḏꜥ 'judge', 'I have judged' (Budge: ut'ā-nà; he prints his English in braces). bgꜣsw is b, a cup sign coded W11 (approximate) for g, ꜣ, the bolt s and w with plural strokes, a plural noun (Budge: beḳasu, 'the guilty'). It is not known elsewhere in these parts; it may belong with bgꜣ 'fault, failing', and the meaning is doubtful. im 'there' is the reed and the owl, the adverb.

sentences.l: (iw) · have-brought-I-him · life · to · nose-his · for · ever
sentences.i: I have brought him life, to his nose, for ever.
sentences.n: iw opens the statement and is not translated. in·n·i is the sign coded W25 (approximate; the house reading for in) with n, then the n of the sḏm·n·f and the seated man: 'I have brought', from ini 'bring'. The horned viper after it is taken, with Budge, as 'him', the one who receives life; the regular object would be the dependent pronoun sw, and the ·f may be a slip for n·f 'to him'. Either way life is brought to him. ꜥnḫ 'life' is the ankh with n and ḫ. r 'to'. fnḏ·f 'his nose' is water n printed over the viper f, then the hand d (for ḏ, as often in later writing), the nose with a stroke, and ·f (Budge: fenṭ-f). n ḏt 'for ever' is the preposition n with ḏt 'everlastingness', the cobra ḏ and t with the land sign. Life is given to the nose as breath.

sentences.i: I am the son of Osiris.
sentences.n: ink 'I am' with the seated man; sꜣ 'son', the duck and its stroke; wsir 'Osiris', the eye and the throne with the seated god, joined to sꜣ as a direct genitive.

sentences.l: have-made-I · the-way · pass-I · by-it · into · the-necropolis
sentences.i: I have made the way, and I pass by it into the necropolis.
sentences.n: ir·n·i 'I have made' is the eye, water n and the seated man, the sḏm·n·f. wꜣt 'the way' is the road sign with t and a stroke. swꜣ·i is the crossed sticks swꜣ with walking legs and ·i: a sḏm·f, 'I pass'. im 'there, by it' is the adverb, a reed and the owl. m 'into'. ẖrt-nṯr 'the necropolis', literally 'what is under the god', is the flag nṯr written first out of respect, a small loop (coded D21, approximate) for r, and the sign ẖr; its t is not written (Budge: Neter-χert). The fourth gate ends here.

sentences.i: The fifth gate.
sentences.n: The papyrus writes these two words in red. This unit opens the fifth gate, and Budge's line numbers start again at 1; the fifth gate runs over his lines 1 to 9. ꜥryt as before. diwnwt 'fifth' is five strokes, two over three, the numeral five (diw), with the pot nw and t: the ordinal diwnw, feminine (Budge: ṭuat).

sentences.i: The name of its doorkeeper: Ankh-ef-em-fenetju.
sentences.n: iry-ꜥꜣ·s as before, here without the low sign U15. The name is three of Budge's groups, joined here as one word: ꜥnḫ·f 'he lives', the ankh with n and ḫ and the viper ·f; m 'on' (the sign Aa15); and fnṯw 'worms', f, water n (restored by Budge inside his square brackets), t for ṯ, a small worm (coded I14, approximate) and plural strokes. 'He lives on worms' (Budge: Ānkh-f-em-fent): a keeper who feeds on the creatures of decay.

sentences.i: The name of its watcher: Shabu.
sentences.n: The papyrus writes rn n in red. sꜣwty·s 'its watcher' as at the first gate. The name is a marsh plant šꜣ (M8; Budge's numeral 4 is printed after it) with ꜣ, b and w, then a tall loop ending in a small bulb (coded V1, approximate) and the seated god (Budge: Śabu). The name is not understood.

sentences.i: The name of the announcer in it: Deb-her-keha-kheft.
sentences.n: The papyrus writes rn n in red. smi im·s 'the announcer in it' as before. The name runs from the foot of Budge's p. 60 to the top of p. 61, in two groups joined here as one word: the hand d and b, the face ḥr with its stroke, the basket k and the shelter h (Budge's numeral 6 between them), ꜣ and a small pair of walking legs, then ḫ, f and t with the seated god (Budge: Ṭeb-ḥrà-keha-χeft). ḥr is 'face' and ḫft may be 'against, opposite' or belong with ḫfty 'enemy'; db and khꜣ are not identified, and the name is not understood.

sentences.l: said · by · the-Osiris · the-scribe · Ani · true-of-voice
sentences.i: Said by the Osiris, the scribe Ani, true of voice:
sentences.n: The papyrus writes ḏd in in red; the rest is black. The words are those of the fourth gate: ḏd in 'said by', the Osiris, the scribe Ani, mꜣꜥ-ḫrw 'true of voice'.

sentences.i: I have brought the two jaws that are in Rosetau.
sentences.n: in·n·i 'I have brought', as at the fourth gate, without the viper. ꜥrty is ꜥ, r, t and two strokes, the dual ending, with two jawbones (coded F19, approximate) as classifiers: ꜥrty 'the two jaws' (Budge: ārti, 'jaw bones'; he supplies 'thy'). imyt is the crossed planks im (Z11) with m and t: the nisba imy 'which is in', in the feminine to agree with ꜥrty (Budge: àmt, 'into'). rꜣ-sṯꜣw 'Rosetau', the mouth with a stroke, the cord sign sṯꜣ (approximate), strokes and the desert sign, as in the first part. At this gate the speaker brings Osiris the parts of his body, one from each holy place.

sentences.l: have-brought-I · for-you · the-back · which-is-in · Heliopolis · uniting · many-its · there
sentences.i: I have brought you the backbone that is in Heliopolis, uniting its many parts there(?).
sentences.n: in·n·i n·k 'I have brought you': n·k is water n and the basket, 'for you', Osiris. psd 'back, backbone' is p, the bolt s and the hand d, with a stroke; its classifier is a disk with hanging rays (coded N8, approximate), the sign of psḏ 'shine', where a sign of the body would be expected (Budge: pesṭ, 'backbone'). imy 'which is in' is the crossed planks with m, masculine to agree with psd. iwnw 'Heliopolis' is the column iwn with the pot nw and the town sign (Budge: Ànnu). dmḏ is a single sign not identified, two hanging cones tied to a crossed square (coded V6, approximate); it is read with Budge (ṭemt) as dmḏ 'unite, join together', and the reading rests on him. ꜥšꜣ·f is the lizard ꜥšꜣ 'many' with plural strokes and ·f: 'its many (parts)', the vertebrae (Budge: āśt-f; his English for these two words is in braces). im 'there'. The second half of the unit is doubtful.

sentences.i: I drive back Apep for you.
sentences.n: The papyrus writes ꜥꜣpp in red, as the name of the enemy of the sun is often written. ḫsf·i is the spindle-and-viper sign ḫsf with the low sign U15 and the seated man: a sḏm·f, 'I drive back' (Budge has 'I have', which would need the n of the sḏm·n·f). n·k 'for you'. ꜥꜣpp 'Apep', the serpent, is a long pointed sign with a small ring (coded O29, approximate) for ꜥꜣ, p twice and the snake.

sentences.i: I have spat on the wounds(?).
sentences.n: The papyrus writes p, g, ꜣ and s; read psg 'spit, spit on', with s and g changed round and an ꜣ added. The classifier is a stream from the lips (coded D26, approximate), the sign of spitting, which leaves only this word; Budge reads peḳas, following the signs as they stand. Then water n and the seated man: psg·n·i 'I have spat'. nsp is water n, a hooked sign under it (coded T14, approximate; one reader took it for the tongue ns), the bolt s and p, with a knife (T30) and plural strokes: a word for cuts or wounds, the knife its classifier (Budge: nesp, 'the cuttings in the flesh'); the hooked sign is not read, and the word is doubtful. Spittle was a remedy: the speaker heals the god's wounds.

sentences.i: I have made a way among you.
sentences.n: ir·n·i 'I have made' is the eye with plural strokes (not read), water n and a single stroke for the seated man ·i, a shorter writing of the suffix. wꜣt 'a way'. imy·tn is the crossed planks im with m and two strokes y, then t and n with plural strokes, the suffix ·tn 'you' (plural): the nisba imy 'which is in, among', 'which is among you', the beings of the gate.

sentences.i: I am the old one among the gods.
sentences.n: ink 'I am', the pot and the basket alone. iꜣw 'old man, the aged one' is the bent man leaning on a stick (A19) with the seated god (Budge: àau, 'the Aged one'). imyt is the crossed planks with m and t: taken as the preposition imytw 'between, among', its w not written (Budge: àmt, 'among'). nṯrw 'the gods' is the flag written three times, the old way of writing a plural. Budge's heading 'PLATE XII.' falls between imyt and nṯrw: the text runs on into Plate 12.

sentences.i: I perform the purification for Osiris(?).
sentences.n: ir·i is the eye with the seated man: a sḏm·f of iri, 'I make, I perform' (Budge: 'I have made'; no n is written). The next word is a single sign, a curved horn crossing a stick (coded F16, approximate), the horn ꜥb: taken as ꜥbw 'purification', its w not written. Budge reads āb, 'the offering', which would be ꜥbt with its t not written; either sense is possible and the reading is doubtful. n 'for' and wsir, the eye and the throne with the seated god; n could also be the genitive, 'the purification of Osiris'.

sentences.i: I have protected him in his vindication.
sentences.n: nḏ is the sign coded Aa27 (approximate; the house reading for nḏ), the pot nw standing for its n, and the low sign U15: nḏ 'protect', the word used of Horus who protects (and avenges) his father. Budge's groups net' and en are joined here into one word, the sḏm·n·f nḏ·n 'I have protected'; its suffix ·i is not written, as often on this papyrus, and is read from the 'I' of the speech. sw 'him' is the sedge sw with w, the dependent pronoun. m mꜣꜥ-ḫrw 'in vindication': m (Aa15) with the noun mꜣꜥ-ḫrw, the plinth and the oar. Budge takes the words as 'he has triumphed', with en as the n of a sḏm·n·f and sw as its subject; that reading is possible, but sw does not usually stand as the subject of a verb.

sentences.i: uniting his bones, gathering his limbs.
sentences.n: dmḏ 'uniting' is the same unidentified sign as in line 7 (coded V6, approximate), read with Budge (ṭemt); the reading rests on him. qsw·f 'his bones' is the harpoon-head qs written three times for the plural, with ·f (Budge: qesu-f). sꜣq 'gather, collect' is the folded cloth s, a box-like sign coded Aa18 (approximate) for sꜣ, ꜣ, the wedge q, a low animal-like sign (coded I3, approximate; not a usual classifier of this word) and the roll (Budge: saqa). ꜥwt·f 'his limbs' is the arm ꜥ and t with a piece of flesh (F51, approximate) and a stroke, and ·f; the plural ending is not written. The two infinitives tell how the speaker has protected Osiris, by putting his body together again. The fifth gate ends here.

sentences.i: The sixth gate.
sentences.n: The papyrus writes these two words in red. This unit opens the sixth gate, at the head of Plate 12, and Budge's line numbers start again at 1; the sixth gate runs over his lines 1 to 9. sisnwt 'sixth' is six strokes, the numeral six (sis), with the pot nw and t: the ordinal sisnw, feminine (Budge: saset).

sentences.i: The name of its doorkeeper: Itek-tau-kehaq-kheru.
sentences.n: iry-ꜥꜣ·s as before. The name is a reed, t and k (itk); t with a pot-shaped vessel (coded U30, approximate; the kiln tꜣ), a loaf (coded X4, approximate) and plural strokes, perhaps tꜣw 'loaves', the loaf as classifier; the basket k, the shelter h (Budge's numeral 3 after it), ꜣ and the wedge q (khꜣq); and the oar ḫrw with w and the man with hand to mouth, 'voice' (Budge: Àtek-tau-kehaq-χeru). Only ḫrw 'voice' is clear, and the name is not understood.

sentences.i: The name of its watcher: In-her.
sentences.n: The papyrus writes rn n in red. sꜣwty·s 'its watcher' as before. The name is the sign coded W25 (approximate) for in, with n, and the face ḥr with its stroke and the seated god (Budge: Àn-ḥrà). If in is the verb ini 'bring, fetch', the name may mean 'Who brings the face' (?); doubtful.

sentences.i: The name of the announcer in it: Ades-her.
sentences.n: The papyrus writes rn n in red. The name runs from Budge's p. 61 to p. 62, in two groups joined here as one word: ꜣ, the hand d and the bolt s with a knife (coded T30) as classifier, then the face ḥr with its stroke and the seated god (Budge: Aṭes-ḥrà). After the seated god come a flat sign with two diagonal strokes (coded X4, approximate) and a second seated god, which Budge does not transliterate: they are not read here, and may be a repeated classifier or a slip. ꜣds is not identified; the knife points to a word of cutting, so perhaps 'Sharp of face' (?), a guess.

sentences.i: Said by the Osiris, the scribe Ani:
sentences.n: The papyrus writes ḏd in in red. 'Said by the Osiris, the scribe Ani', as at the fourth and fifth gates, here without mꜣꜥ-ḫrw.

sentences.i: I have come today! I have come today!
sentences.n: ii·n·i 'I have come' is the sign ii (M18) with a reed and walking legs, then water n and the seated man, the sḏm·n·f of ii 'come'. min 'today' is the milk jug mi (W19) with n and the sun as classifier (Budge: mān, 'daily'). sp sn 'twice' is a circle with marks inside (coded O50, the threshing floor sp, 'time, occasion') and two strokes, the numeral two: a note to the reader to say the words two times.

sentences.i: I have made the way of my going, which Anubis created(?).
sentences.n: ir·n·i wꜣt 'I have made the way', as at the fifth gate. šmt·i is a pool on walking legs printed as one sign (the sign šm, N40; coded here as the pool N37 and the legs), with m, t, walking legs again and the seated man: the infinitive šmt 'going' with ·i, 'my going', joined to wꜣt as a direct genitive (Budge: śemt-à, 'I have passed along'). Budge's groups qemam and en are joined here into one word: the wedge q and ꜣ, a throw-stick (coded T14, approximate), the sign of qmꜣ 'create', with m (Aa15) and a clump of plants (coded M15, approximate) as classifier, then water n: the relative form qmꜣ·n 'which (Anubis) created'. The plant classifier belongs rather to qmꜣ 'reed, rush', a word of the same sound. inpw 'Anubis' is a reed, n and p with the seated jackal-headed god. The relative form would take a t to agree with wꜣt, which is not written; the construction is doubtful, and 'my going' may also be a clause of its own, 'I go …'.

sentences.l: I · the-lord · of-the-Great-Crown · who-devises(?) · magic · the-protector · of-maat
sentences.i: I am the lord of the Great Crown, who devises(?) magic, the protector of maat.
sentences.n: ink 'I am'. nb 'the lord', the basket. wrrt 'the Great Crown' is the swallow wr with r twice and a crown (coded S3, approximate; Budge's numeral 8 before it) as classifier; the t is not written. ḫmt is ḫ, the hooked sign mt (D53, the house reading), t, three lines (Z3A) and the arms held out (D35, approximate), as in the third gate: ḫmt 'think out, plan', taken as a participle, 'who devises'. Budge reads 'without' (χemet), as though from ḫm 'not know', whose classifier the arms are; the word is doubtful. ḥkꜣw 'magic, spells' is the wick ḥ, the raised arms kꜣ, the coil w, ꜣ and the man with hand to mouth with a stroke (Budge: ḥekau). nḏ is the sign coded Aa27 with the pot for its n and U15, here a participle used as a noun, 'the protector' (Budge: net'); mꜣꜥt 'maat, right order' is the sickle mꜣ, the arm ꜥ and t, with the plinth (Aa11), the roll and a stroke as classifiers.

sentences.i: I have protected his eye.
sentences.n: nḏ·n·i 'I have protected', the same sign group with water n and the seated man: the sḏm·n·f. irt·f 'his eye' is the eye with t and a stroke, and ·f (Budge: maat-f). The eye is the eye of Horus, wounded and made whole, the type of everything restored to Osiris.

sentences.i: I have bound up(?) the eye of Osiris for him.
sentences.n: sšd·n·i is a looped cord (coded V6, approximate), the hand d and the low sign U15, with water n and the seated man: the sḏm·n·f of the word read sšd with Budge (seśeṭ), left untranslated at the second gate. Here Budge gives 'bandaged', and 'bind up' fits an eye, a thing bound with a band; the sense is a guess. irt n 'the eye of' is restored by Budge inside his square brackets; the genitive is written n, though irt is feminine. wsir 'Osiris', the throne and the eye. n·f 'for him'.

sentences.l: has-been-made · the-way · going · the-Osiris · Ani · with-you · in · […]
sentences.i: The way has been made; the Osiris Ani goes with you in […]
sentences.n: iry is the eye with two reeds and a stroke: taken as the passive sḏm of iri, with its y written, 'has been made' (Budge: àriu, '[I have] made'). wꜣt 'the way'. šmt is the pool-and-legs sign with m, t and walking legs, as in line 7: the infinitive 'going', with the Osiris Ani as its subject (Budge: śemt). ḥnꜥ·tn 'with you' is the twisted wick ḥ, n and ꜥ, with t, n and plural strokes, the suffix ·tn (plural): the beings of the gate. m 'in' (Aa15). After m Budge prints a row of dots: the words that follow are lost or were not given, and the sentence breaks off. The sixth gate ends here.

sentences.i: The seventh gate.
sentences.n: The papyrus writes these two words in red. This unit opens the seventh and last gate, and Budge's line numbers start again at 1; the seventh gate runs over his lines 1 to 8. sfḫnwt 'seventh' is seven strokes, three over three and one, the numeral seven (sfḫ), with the pot nw: the ordinal sfḫnw. The seventh stroke is restored by Budge inside his square brackets, and the feminine t is not written (Budge: seχef).

sentences.i: The name of its doorkeeper: Sekhem-em-denu-sen.
sentences.n: iry-ꜥꜣ·s as before. The name is two of Budge's groups, joined here as one word. The sceptre sḫm with m gives sḫm 'be mighty, have power'. Then come the low sign U15 and t, which are not read here (Budge begins his second group with them, 'Ma-'); the owl m, 'in'; the hand d, under which Budge prints '(sic)', water n and w (Budge's numeral 3 before w), with a knife (T30) and strokes, perhaps dnw 'cutting off', from dn 'sever'; and s and n with strokes, the suffix ·sn 'their'. 'Mighty in cutting them down' (?) (Budge: Seχem-Maṭenu-sen). The unread signs and Budge's sic leave the name doubtful.

sentences.i: The name of its watcher: Aa-maa-kheru.
sentences.n: The papyrus writes rn n in red. The name is a horizontal column-like sign with a knob (coded O29, approximate) for ꜥꜣ, with the arm ꜥ; a flat sign with a small mark on top (coded Aa11, approximate), not read, perhaps the plinth written twice; the plinth mꜣꜥ and the oar ḫrw, and the seated god (Budge: Āā-maāχeru). ꜥꜣ is 'great' and mꜣꜥ-ḫrw 'true of voice': 'Great one, true of voice' (?).

sentences.i: The name of the announcer in it: Khesef-khemiu.
sentences.n: The papyrus writes rn n in red. Between smi and im·s stands a second water n (Budge: 'who [is]'): taken as the genitive n, 'the announcer of (the one) in it', or repeated by slip from rn n; it is not rendered in the English. The name is ḫsf 'repel' (U35 with U15), then ḫ, m and two reeds, with a man pushing over a wall (one sign, coded O36 and A24, approximate) and the seated god with a stroke as classifiers: ḫmiw 'destroyers', from ḫmi 'destroy', of which the toppled wall is the classifier. 'Who repels the destroyers' (Budge: χesef-χemi).

sentences.i: Said by the Osiris Ani:
sentences.n: The papyrus writes ḏd in in red. 'Said by the Osiris Ani', as at the earlier gates.

sentences.i: I have come to you, Osiris, cleansed of the efflux.
sentences.n: ii·n·i ḫr·k wsir 'I have come to you, Osiris', as at the first gate. wꜥb is the leg under a jet of water (D60) with three water lines: the stative 'pure, cleansed'. rḏwt is r, the mountain ḏw, t and w, with a round sign with a curl (coded Aa2, approximate) and a stroke: rḏw 'efflux', the fluid that runs from a corpse, as at the first gate, here with a t (Budge: erṭut, 'emanations'). There the preposition r 'from' was written before it; here it is not, and the single r may stand for both. The signs could also be read r ḏwt, 'pure from evil'; the reading follows the first gate.

sentences.l: go-round-you · the-sky · see-you · Ra · see-you · the-common-folk
sentences.i: You go round the sky, you see Ra, you see the common folk.
sentences.n: rr·k 'you go round' is the long loop (coded V10, approximate), r and walking legs with ·k, as at the first gate; pt 'the sky'. mꜣꜣ·k 'you see' is the eye joined with the sickle mꜣ in one sign, the sickle giving the sound and the eye the classifier, with ·k; in the second mꜣꜣ·k the ·k is restored by Budge inside his square brackets. rꜥ 'Ra' is the seated god with the sun on his head. rḫyt 'the common folk' is the lapwing with t and plural strokes. The words to the god in the first gate come back here.

sentences.i: O sole one, see, you are in the Sektet bark.
sentences.n: wꜥ 'one' is a harpoon sign (coded T21, approximate) for wꜥ, a stroke and the arm ꜥ: taken as an address, 'O sole one' (Budge: uā, 'Only One'); it could also close the sentence before. is·k is a reed and the folded cloth s with ·k: is, a short form of the particle ist 'see, now', with its suffix, followed by m and a noun: 'see, you are in …'. sktt is the bolt s, k, t twice and a boat (coded P3, approximate): the Sektet, the bark in which the sun crosses the sky (Budge: sektet).

sentences.i: He goes round the horizon of the sky.
sentences.n: rr·f 'he goes round', the same verb with ·f. ꜣḫt 'the horizon' is the sun between two hills (N27) with t and the house sign as classifier; nt 'of', feminine to agree with ꜣḫt; pt 'the sky'. The text turns from 'you' to 'he', perhaps Ra in his bark; who is meant is not certain.

sentences.i: I say what I wish to his noble body.
sentences.n: ḏd·i 'I say' is the cobra over the hand (here two separate signs) with the seated man. mrt·i is the hoe mr (coded U6) with r and t, the man with hand to mouth and the seated man ·i: the relative form of mri 'wish', 'what I wish'. n 'to'. sꜥḥ·f is the bolt s, the arm ꜥ and the wick ḥ, with a loop on a small block (coded V39, approximate) as classifier, and ·f: sꜥḥ 'noble', here the noble form of the dead god, his mummy (Budge: sāḥ-f, 'his mummy').

sentences.i: He grows strong; he comes into being as he says.
sentences.n: wsr·f is the head and neck of an animal, wsr (F12), with s, r and the low sign U15, and ·f: a sḏm·f, 'he is strong, grows strong'. ḫpr·f is the scarab ḫpr with r and ·f, 'he comes into being'. mi 'as, according to' is the milk jug mi with a reed. ḏd·f 'he says'. 'He' may be the god whose body the speaker addresses, coming to life at his word. Budge's footnote 1, which gives the passage from another papyrus, is not part of Ani's text and is left out.

sentences.i: You drive back his face.
sentences.n: ḫsf·k is the spindle-and-viper sign ḫsf with U15 and ·k: a sḏm·f, 'you drive back'. ḥr·f 'his face' is the face with its stroke and ·f. To drive back someone's face is to turn him away; who is turned away is not said, perhaps the enemy of the god.

sentences.l: have-made-you · for-me · ways · all · good · before-you
sentences.i: You have made all the ways good for me before you.
sentences.n: ir·n·k is the eye, water n and ·k: the sḏm·n·f of iri, 'you have made'. Budge reads a request ('make'), which would want the imperative or a sḏm·f; as written it is a statement. n·i 'for me' is water n and the seated man. wꜣwt 'ways' is the road sign with t and plural strokes; nbt 'all' is the basket with t, and nfrt 'good' the lute nfr (F35) with f, r and t, both feminine to agree with wꜣwt. nfrt may describe the ways ('all good ways') or say what they are made ('made good'). ḫr·k 'before you', as in line 6. Spell 147 ends here; Spell 146 follows on the papyrus, in the next part.
